events.title: Nabonassar becomes king of Babylon, by Ptolemy's reckoning
events.description: By Ptolemy's reckoning, Nabonassar became king of Babylon. Ptolemy's list of kings, used by later astronomers, counted its years from his accession, and the Babylonian Chronicle also began with his reign.
events.html: By Ptolemy's reckoning, Nabonassar became king of Babylon. Ptolemy's list of kings, used by later astronomers, counted its years from his accession, and the Babylonian Chronicle also began with his reign.

events.title: Valentinian I proclaimed Roman Emperor
events.description: Army officers chose Valentinian, a Pannonian general, as emperor at Nicaea. A month later he made his brother Valens co-emperor in the East, while he ruled the West.
events.html: Army officers chose Valentinian, a Pannonian general, as emperor at Nicaea. A month later he made his brother Valens co-emperor in the East, while he ruled the West.

events.title: King Solomon of Hungary defeats his cousin Duke Géza at Kemej
events.description: Near Kemej, in present-day Heves County, the royal army of King Solomon of Hungary defeated his rebellious cousin Duke Géza, who had been betrayed but escaped. Géza defeated Solomon at Mogyoród that same year and became king.
events.html: Near Kemej, in present-day Heves County, the royal army of King Solomon of Hungary defeated his rebellious cousin Duke Géza, who had been betrayed but escaped. Géza defeated Solomon at Mogyoród that same year and became king.

events.title: Charles of Anjou defeats and kills Manfred at Benevento
events.description: Near Benevento in southern Italy, the army of Charles I of Anjou defeated Manfred, King of Sicily, who was killed in the battle. The victory gave Charles the Kingdom of Sicily and ended Hohenstaufen power in southern Italy.
events.html: Near Benevento in southern Italy, the army of Charles I of Anjou defeated Manfred, King of Sicily, who was killed in the battle. The victory gave Charles the Kingdom of Sicily and ended Hohenstaufen power in southern Italy.

events.title: Galileo is warned to abandon Copernican theory
events.description: Cardinal Bellarmine instructed Galileo, on the Pope's orders, not to hold or defend the view that the Earth moves around the Sun. His 1632 'Dialogue' led to his trial for breaching the order.
events.html: Cardinal Bellarmine instructed Galileo, on the Pope's orders, not to hold or defend the view that the Earth moves around the Sun. His 1632 'Dialogue' led to his trial for breaching the order.

events.title: Napoleon escapes from Elba
events.description: With about a thousand men, Napoleon slipped away from his island exile and sailed for France. He regained power without a shot, beginning the Hundred Days that ended at Waterloo.
events.html: With about a thousand men, Napoleon slipped away from his island exile and sailed for France. He regained power without a shot, beginning the Hundred Days that ended at Waterloo.

events.title: Grand Canyon becomes a US national park
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson signed the act creating Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona. The gorge, carved by the Colorado River, is over 1.6 km deep in places.
events.html: President Woodrow Wilson signed the act creating Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona. The gorge, carved by the Colorado River, is over 1.6 km deep in places.

events.title: Robert Watson-Watt's team demonstrates radar
events.description: At Daventry, radio waves from a BBC transmitter bounced off an RAF bomber and were detected on a screen. The test led to the Chain Home network, vital in the Battle of Britain.
events.html: At Daventry, radio waves from a BBC transmitter bounced off an RAF bomber and were detected on a screen. The test led to the Chain Home network, vital in the Battle of Britain.

events.title: Truck bomb explodes beneath the World Trade Center
events.description: Islamist militants detonated a bomb in the North Tower's underground car park, killing six people and injuring more than 1,000. The towers survived but were destroyed in the attacks of 2001.
